title: 2. Cell: the Building Block of Life

q.t: The limit of resolution of the human eye is…
1 mm = how many µm?
Total magnification = ?
Diffusion of water across a selectively permeable membrane is…
Cells with no well-defined nucleus are…
The powerhouse of the cell is the…
Rough ER has ___ attached.
Colourless plastids that store starch are…
Cell division giving gametes with half the chromosomes is…
q.e: Mitosis keeps the number the same.

q.t: Who proposed that new cells form only from pre-existing cells (1855)?
A potato piece in plain water…
A potato piece in 20% salt solution…
q.e: Water leaves towards the more concentrated side.

q.t: In osmosis, water moves towards…
Why do plants need a cell wall?
o: They can't move, so need rigidity against wind and rain

q.t: Smooth ER makes and stores…
Chromoplasts give flowers and fruits bright colours to…
Why do mature human RBCs have no nucleus?
o: To hold more haemoglobin and carry more oxygen
q.e: The cost: they can't divide or repair.

q.t: Why do plants wilt without water?
o: Vacuoles lose water and cell pressure drops
q.e: The vacuole keeps the cell firm.

q.t: Body growth happens mainly by…
q.e: Cells can only grow to a certain size.

q.t: Schleiden (1838) showed ___ are made of cells.
Why does a cell have many small mitochondria rather than one giant one?
o: Many small ones give more total membrane area
q.e: More surface area, more energy production.

q.t: Why are mitochondrial cristae folded?
o: To increase surface area for reactions
q.e: More reaction space in the same volume.

q.t: Mitochondria and plastids have their own DNA. This suggests…
o: They were once free-living single-celled organisms

q.t: Why is magnification without resolution useless?
o: Enlarging a blur only gives a bigger blur

q.t: Why do chromosomes condense only at division?
o: Loose thread is easy to read but hard to share out
q.e: Winding makes them easy to separate.

q.t: Why must gametes have half the chromosomes?
o: Otherwise every generation would double the number
q.e: Two halves make a full set.

q.t: Contact inhibition means…
o: Division stops when cells touch neighbours

q.t: Programmed cell death in the embryo forms…
o: Fingers, by removing cells between them
q.e: Without it we'd have webbed hands.

q.t: Plant cell shrinks in salt solution but keeps its outer shape because…
o: The rigid cell wall holds the shape
q.e: Only membrane and cytoplasm pull inward.

q.t: Venter's synthetic-DNA experiment showed…
o: DNA controls a cell's structure and activities
A cell was created from scratch

q.t: Eyepiece 10× and objective 40×. Total magnification?
Eyepiece 15× and objective 10×. Total magnification?
10 cells sit side by side across 0.5 mm. Width of one cell (µm)?
Why weigh potato pieces before the osmosis experiment?
o: The change in weight is the result
q.e: Equal starting sizes make changes comparable.

q.t: Why look at the root TIP for dividing cells?
q.e: Squashing spreads the cells for viewing.

q.t: Totipotency (Haberlandt, 1902) means…
o: Any living plant cell can grow into a whole plant
q.e: The basis of plant tissue culture.

q.t: Errors in meiosis can cause…
Do plant cells show contact inhibition?
o: No — rigid walls give a different growth pattern

q.t: Lysosomal enzymes in sperm help by…
o: Breaking down the egg's outer layer

q.t: Why have organelles at all?
o: So many processes can run at once in separate compartments
q.e: A cell is like a tiny factory.
